What We Do

[/et_pb_text][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” text_font=”Source Sans Pro|600|||||||” text_text_color=”#000000″ text_font_size=”16px” text_font_size_tablet=”16px” text_font_size_phone=”17px” text_font_size_last_edited=”on|phone” text_orientation_tablet=”” text_orientation_phone=”center” text_orientation_last_edited=”on|phone” global_colors_info=”{}”]

At Fox Septic Pumping, we understand how important a well-maintained septic system is to your home or business. Regular pumping is essential to prevent backups, foul odors, and costly repairs, and our experienced team is here to make that process simple and stress-free. With over 15 years of experience, we’ve built a reputation for providing reliable, thorough, and honest service that keeps your system running clean and efficient year-round.

Our skilled technicians use professional-grade equipment to completely remove waste buildup and sludge, helping your tank operate properly and extending its lifespan. During each service, we take the time to inspect your system for any potential issues, ensuring that small problems are addressed before they turn into big ones. Whether you’re on a regular maintenance schedule or need emergency pumping, you can count on us for prompt response times, quality workmanship, and friendly service from start to finish.

As a locally owned and operated company, we take pride in treating every customer like a neighbor and every property like our own. We leave your space clean, your system performing at its best, and your mind at ease. When you choose Fox Septic Pumping, you’re choosing dependable care from a team that values integrity, professionalism, and long-term peace of mind for you and your family.

Know Your Septic System

At Fox Septic Pumping, we know that septic systems can be confusing, and questions are normal. Our goal is to provide clear, helpful answers so you understand your system, the services we provide, and how to keep everything running smoothly. Below, you’ll find answers to some of the most common questions our customers ask.

[/et_pb_text][/et_pb_column][et_pb_column type=”1_2″ specialty_columns=”2″ _builder_version=”4.16″ custom_padding=”|||” global_colors_info=”{}” custom_padding__hover=”|||”][et_pb_row_inner column_structure=”1_2,1_2″ use_custom_gutter=”on” gutter_width=”2″ _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” custom_padding=”0px||0px||true|false” locked=”off” global_colors_info=”{}”][et_pb_column_inner type=”1_2″ saved_specialty_column_type=”1_2″ _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}”][et_pb_blurb title=”How often should I have my septic tank pumped?” _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” header_font=”Merriweather|700|||||||” header_font_size=”20px” header_letter_spacing=”1px” body_font=”Source Sans Pro|600|||||||” body_text_color=”#000000″ body_font_size=”16px” background_color=”#F8F8F8″ custom_padding=”15px|15px|15px|15px|true|true” border_width_all=”3px” border_color_all=”#EE1C25″ locked=”off” global_colors_info=”{}”]

In most cases, septic tanks should be pumped every 3 to 5 years, depending on the size of the tank, number of people in the household, and water usage. Regular maintenance helps prevent system overload, backups, and expensive repairs.

[/et_pb_blurb][/et_pb_column_inner][et_pb_column_inner type=”1_2″ saved_specialty_column_type=”1_2″ _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}”][et_pb_blurb title=”What happens during a septic pumping service?” _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” header_font=”Merriweather|700|||||||” header_font_size=”20px” header_letter_spacing=”1px” body_font=”Source Sans Pro|600|||||||” body_text_color=”#000000″ body_font_size=”16px” background_color=”#F8F8F8″ custom_padding=”15px|15px|15px|15px|true|true” border_width_all=”3px” border_color_all=”#EE1C25″ locked=”off” global_colors_info=”{}”]

Our technicians locate and uncover the tank lids, safely remove all waste using our pumping equipment, and check for any signs of cracks, leaks, or blockages. We make sure the tank is completely cleaned out before securely closing.

[/et_pb_blurb][/et_pb_column_inner][/et_pb_row_inner][et_pb_row_inner column_structure=”1_2,1_2″ use_custom_gutter=”on” gutter_width=”2″ _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” custom_padding=”30px||30px||true|false” locked=”off” global_colors_info=”{}”][et_pb_column_inner type=”1_2″ saved_specialty_column_type=”1_2″ _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}”][et_pb_blurb title=”What happens if I don’t pump my septic tank regularly?” _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” header_font=”Merriweather|700|||||||” header_font_size=”20px” header_letter_spacing=”1px” body_font=”Source Sans Pro|600|||||||” body_text_color=”#000000″ body_font_size=”15px” background_color=”#F8F8F8″ custom_padding=”15px|15px|15px|15px|true|true” border_width_all=”3px” border_color_all=”#EE1C25″ locked=”off” global_colors_info=”{}”]

Over time, solids build up in your tank, reducing its capacity and potentially pushing waste into the drain field. This can cause backups, system failure, and costly damage. Routine pumping keeps your septic system healthy and working properly.

[/et_pb_blurb][/et_pb_column_inner][et_pb_column_inner type=”1_2″ saved_specialty_column_type=”1_2″ _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}”][et_pb_blurb title=”What are the signs that my septic tank needs pumping?” _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” header_font=”Merriweather|700|||||||” header_font_size=”20px” header_letter_spacing=”1px” body_font=”Source Sans Pro|600|||||||” body_text_color=”#000000″ body_font_size=”15px” background_color=”#F8F8F8″ custom_padding=”15px|15px|15px|15px|true|true” border_width_all=”3px” border_color_all=”#EE1C25″ locked=”off” global_colors_info=”{}”]

Common signs include slow drains, foul odors, gurgling sounds in your plumbing, or standing water near your drain field. If you notice any of these symptoms, it’s best to have your system inspected and pumped as soon as possible.

[/et_pb_blurb][/et_pb_column_inner][/et_pb_row_inner][/et_pb_column][/et_pb_section]
